item.title: On This Day: Irish filmmaker Neil Jordan was born in Sligo, in 1950
item.description: Celebrating the life and huge body of work of Neil Jordan, from "The Crying Game" to "Riviera".

item.title: Symbol of Ireland: the Irish harp's sweet music and myth
item.description: With its history rooted in ancient Irish history and lore there's more than magical music to the Irish harp.

item.title: WATCH: The Irish invented battery-powered trains 85 years before Tesla
item.description: An Irish chemist named Dr. James J. Drumm created battery-powered trains, which successfully operated on a Dublin to Bray route from 1932 to 1948.

item.title: On This Day: The fiercest blizzard of the 'Big Snow' of 1947 hit Ireland
item.description: 'The Blizzard' of February 25th was the greatest single snowfall on record and lasted for close on 50 consecutive hours.

item.title: Phoenix Irish Cultural Center and McClelland Library hires new Executive Director
item.description: Dr. Hofmann-Handy secures position as the organization prepares for Irish-American Heritage Month and its St. Patrick’s Day festivities.

item.title: Bringing the beauty of Killarney to the world with Mucros Weavers
item.description: Discover how a historic workshop in the heart of County Kerry uses centuries of tradition to create timeless Irish textiles for a global audience.

item.title: Strong growth sees Irish company Stripe significantly increase valuation
item.description: Stripe has signed agreements with investors to provide liquidity to current and former employees through a tender offer valuing the company at $159bn (€135bn) - a 70% increase.

item.title: Nikita Hand to be paid damages by couple who ‘lied’ about seeing boyfriend attack her
item.description: Nikita Hand has won a court judgment and will now be awarded damages against a couple she said falsely claimed to have seen her being attacked by her partner.

item.title: Thousands raised for ICE detainee Séamus Culleton drawn down
item.description: Money raised by a GoFundMe page for ICE detainee Séamus Culleton has been withdrawn, and the page closed, Extra.ie has learned.

item.title: "Nothing short of epic" Irish hotel awarded double five-star Forbes rating
item.description: The staff at Ashford Castle are "in seventh heaven" after being awarded a double five-star Forbes rating.
